items.followUp: Define an ionic bond and give one example.

rubric.why: A covalent bond is defined by sharing electrons between atoms.
rubric.description: Defines a covalent bond as a bond formed by sharing electron pairs between atoms.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that atoms share electrons or electron pairs to form the bond.

rubric.why: A single covalent bond involves one shared pair of electrons.
rubric.description: Identifies a single covalent bond and gives an example.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the type and a suitable example.

rubric.why: A double covalent bond involves two shared pairs of electrons.
rubric.description: Identifies a double covalent bond and gives an example.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the type and a suitable example.

rubric.why: A triple covalent bond involves three shared pairs of electrons.
rubric.description: Identifies a triple covalent bond and gives an example.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the type and a suitable example.

modelAnswer: A covalent bond is formed when two atoms share one or more pairs of electrons.
A single covalent bond has one shared pair of electrons; for example, H₂.
A double covalent bond has two shared pairs of electrons; for example, O₂.
A triple covalent bond has three shared pairs of electrons; for example, N₂.

items.followUp: Explain diffusion in gases and state two factors that affect its rate.

rubric.why: Diffusion is the intermixing or spreading of particles.
rubric.description: Defines diffusion in liquids as the spreading or intermixing of particles.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for describing particles spreading or mixing.

rubric.why: Diffusion occurs down a concentration gradient.
rubric.description: States that particles move from a region of higher concentration to one of lower concentration.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for correctly stating the direction of movement.

rubric.why: Increasing temperature gives particles more kinetic energy and increases diffusion rate.
rubric.description: Explains the effect of temperature on diffusion in liquids.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that higher temperature increases the rate.

rubric.why: The concentration difference and particle size influence the rate of diffusion.
rubric.description: Gives another relevant factor affecting diffusion rate.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that a greater concentration difference or smaller particles increase the rate.

modelAnswer: Diffusion in liquids is the intermixing of liquid particles as they move from a region of higher concentration to a region of lower concentration.
Diffusion in liquids is slower than in gases because liquid particles are closer together.
An increase in temperature increases the particles’ kinetic energy and speeds up diffusion.
A greater concentration difference increases the rate of diffusion; smaller particles also diffuse faster.

items.followUp: How many particles are present in one mole of a substance? Give the value.

rubric.why: Avogadro’s number is the number of particles in one mole.
rubric.description: Gives the value of Avogadro’s number.

rubric.why: Nₐ is the standard symbol for Avogadro’s number.
rubric.description: Gives the symbol of Avogadro’s number.

modelAnswer: Avogadro’s number is the number of particles present in one mole of a substance.
Its symbol is Nₐ, and its value is 6.02 × 10²³ mol⁻¹.

rubric.why: The periodic function describes the regular repetition of properties with atomic number.
rubric.description: Explains that elemental properties repeat periodically when arranged by increasing atomic number.
rubric.how: Award 2 marks for relating periodic repetition of properties to atomic number.

modelAnswer: A property is a periodic function of atomic number if it repeats at regular intervals as atomic number increases.
Thus, the properties of elements recur periodically when the elements are arranged in order of increasing atomic number.
